Subject: Nimbus Security Questionnaire — Data residency & retention (Hosted API)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking this — attached is our standard security questionnaire (focused on residency, retention, and deletion for hosted APIs). We have a couple of customers in regulated finance who are gating on clear answers here. Can you confirm the following at a high level and, if possible, provide evidence:

1) Where customer data is hosted (region options) and how we guarantee region-specific routing.
2) Retention windows for: a) ephemeral request cache / KV cache, b) request/response logs, c) backups and snapshots.
3) Tenant data erasure workflow and observable evidence (audit logs) when a customer requests deletion.
4) If data is removed from hot storage, how long does it remain in backups/replicas and what is the process to remove it?
5) Any limitations (e.g., data in third-party monitoring/analytics) we should be aware of.

We need answers and supporting artifacts (playbook snippets, sample audit logs) by end of week to move forward. Attaching: nimbus_sq_v3.pdf (your reference includes our required fields).

Appreciate it — Evan

Hi Evan — thanks for the questionnaire and context. High-level answers below; attached is a short artifact bundle that maps directly to the questions in your PDF (file: redwood_answers_nimbus_v1.pdf). If you need deeper technical artifacts (config snippets, logs), Ben and Marissa are looped in and can provide samples.

Quick summary (hosted API):
- Region options: Customers may choose us-west-2 (Oregon), us-east-1 (N. Virginia), eu-west-1 (Ireland). Requests are routed by policy; we support region pinning at the account level and will only serve data in the selected region for hosted tenants.
- Retention:
  • Ephemeral KV/cache: auto-evicted within 48 hours of inactivity; active caches are not persisted to disk.
  • Request/response logs (used for debugging & billing): default 30 days; configurable per-account down to 0 days for strict customers.
  • Backups & snapshots: incremental backups retained for 90 days; full nightly snapshots retained for 30 days. Backups are immutable but we offer targeted restore/expunge workflows (see erasure workflow below).
- Tenant erasure workflow: customer submits deletion request via Console or API -> ticket created -> system triggers soft-delete (flags records) within 24 hours -> background job removes data from hot stores within 48 hours -> deletion from snapshots/backups is handled asynchronously and completed (or scheduled) within 30 days (policy: 30 days to allow in-flight restores). We capture audit logs for each step (who/when/action).
- Backups/replicas: backups are stored with retention metadata. When a targeted erasure is requested, we schedule removal from backups and mark affected backups for redaction; redaction completes within 30 days. For forensic needs we provide attestations and sample redaction logs.
- Third-party telemetry: minimal — we emit aggregated usage metrics to a monitoring provider (team-level metrics only). No PII or prompt/response content is sent to third-party analytics by default; customers can opt in to additional telemetry.

Next steps: I attached a two-page answer mapping and a sample playbook excerpt for tenant erasure. Ben — can you attach the erasure playbook and an anonymized sample audit log we can share? Marissa — can you confirm the default retention config for new accounts?

Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the items.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Security & Privacy PM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_answers_nimbus_v1.pdf (pdf - summary answers)

If accelerating to 7 days isn’t possible, please indicate the blockers (technical, legal, operational).

Thanks — Evan

Evan — quick update and concrete artifacts attached.

1) Accelerated purge: We can support a 7-day accelerated purge SLA for hosted customers under a commercial addendum. Operationally this requires: a) a retention-addendum on contract, b) approval from our infra team to run expedited backup redaction jobs, and c) a brief scheduling window to coordinate snapshot redaction. The blockers are primarily operational (coordination and ensuring no unintended data loss for shared snapshot chains).

2) Evidence: attached two artifacts — tenant-erasure-playbook.pdf (playbook excerpt showing steps and owner roles) and s3-deletion-evidence-sample.txt (anonymized deletion/audit log entry). Below is an anonymized sample audit entry (also in the txt):

  {
    "timestamp": "2027-06-22T14:02:33Z",
    "tenant_id": "redacted-tenant-xxxx",
    "action": "tenant_deletion_request",
    "actor": "security@nimbuslabs.com",
    "status": "completed:hot-delete",
    "hot_delete_completed_at": "2027-06-22T14:45:12Z",
    "backup_redaction_scheduled_at": "2027-06-22T15:00:00Z"
  }

3) Example ticket: see playbook attachment for a redacted ticket flow; we can also provide a template export from our ticketing system (redacted) if needed.

If you want the 7-day SLA we will surface a pricing addendum and an operational checklist. Otherwise the standard flow is 30 days for backup redaction. Let me know which path you prefer and we’ll produce a signed addendum.

—Aisha
